comparison.contamination_hypothesis: REFUTED — clean from-scratch run reproduces reported cycle-002 H3 composite to within 0.1%, indicating cycle-002 H3's reported number (0.04420) is valid project-best despite the suspect train_seconds=25.0 logged value. The contamination concern raised in cycle-003 was a non-issue for the cycle-002 H3 baseline.

training_evidence.note_on_poisson_149s: Poisson trained for 149s vs Heat's 477s — 3.2x faster on the same model. May reflect dataset shape differences (fewer effective LF batches per epoch or smaller train split) rather than contamination. Both datasets ran cache=miss with cuda device — no resume was possible since checkpoints/fno_coreg_residual/ was emptied prior to the run. The cycle-003 H1 Poisson took 549s under the (2.0, 0.25) loss-weighting recipe; the 3.7x gap to the 149s here is consistent with the recipe changing the gradient/step compute profile, not with contamination.

interpretation: The cycle-004 BASELINE is established at composite_nRMSE = 0.04415, essentially identical to the cycle-002 H3 reported number (0.04420, delta 0.1%). The contamination concern from cycle-003's retrospective is REFUTED — cycle-002 H3 was a valid project-best. The cycle-004 bar to beat is therefore 0.04415 (or equivalently, the rounded 0.0442). Per-dataset bars: ifc_heat already beats paper by 2.82x (no upside expected from cycle-004 improvements there); ifc_poisson remains at 0.0742, 1.66x worse than paper bar 0.036 and worse than cycle-002 H4's 0.0596 on the simpler fno_mf_stack backbone. The dominant cycle-004 failure mode is ifc_poisson on the fno_coreg_residual backbone — same as cycle-003 H1 entry, but cycle-003 H1 tried a static (2.0, 0.25) recipe and was refuted. Cycle-003 close-out pre-registered two cycle-004 directions: (a) adaptive loss-weighting (GradNorm-lite, uncertainty-weighted, PCGrad); (b) gentler static asymmetry (e.g. 1.5, 0.5) tuned per backbone. A third option is architectural: per-dataset capacity / modes override or basis-head calibration probe.
